subject: POC prompt & log collection — eval acceptance criteria and next steps (Skyline Health)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + ask: prompt/log collection for the POC evaluation (next steps)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Short recap and a concrete ask to keep the POC moving:

Key objective: validate Redwood inference on Skyline Health triage queries for clinical intake to show parity vs your current rules engine on accuracy and latency under realistic traffic.

What we discussed (brief):
- Scope: ~2k representative user queries (prompts) across triage, benefit eligibility, and appointment scheduling.
- Evaluation: holdout set (20%) for final acceptance; automated rubric + manual spot-checks.
- Success criteria: >=92% accuracy on intent classification, median 150–200ms token latency, and no PII in prompts beyond those allowed per SOW.
- Security: data to be delivered to our dedicated S3 bucket (private endpoint, bucket policy + KMS).

Concrete ask from you: share a single CSV (sample_prompts_20280214.csv) with these columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_intent, expected_entity_count, redaction_flag. We also requested a small system sample logs archive (sys_logs_jan-feb-2028.tar.gz) for load profile and token distribution.

Upload options (pick one):
1) Share a pre-signed S3 path we provide (preferred)
2) Upload to the Drive folder I created and share link

Next conv: proposed intake checkpoint on Tue 2/21 to confirm dataset arrived and outline eval owner roles.

Owners on our side:
- Marcus Lin (eng lead) — eval design, model config
- Ben Carter (solutions) — prompts QA & acceptance tests
- Naomi Feldman (CS) — success criteria and customer coordination

Anything you want us to adjust in the acceptance criteria before we send the S3 details?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prompt template stub (CSV columns described above)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skylinehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev-ops@skylinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: prompt/log collection for the POC evaluation (next steps)

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and a couple of clarifications: 

- We can deliver ~2.5k prompts in the CSV and will mark PII with redaction_flag. Our legal team asked that any PHI be removed before transfer; we will sanitize patient identifiers but keep medical terms and appointment context.
- For the expected_intent column, we have an internal taxonomy (levels 1–3). We'll map to your intents where possible and include the mapping table in the Drive folder.
- DevOps will upload the sys logs to an S3 staging location but need your pre-signed path.

Question: for manual spot-checks, what fraction do you typically review? Also confirm whether the 20% holdout should be random or stratified by intent?

We aim to have the CSV and logs uploaded by Thu 2/17 EOD. Can you send the pre-signed S3 details today?

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Director, Product Operations
Skyline Health

Attachment: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: prompt/log collection for the POC evaluation (next steps)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks — sending pre-signed S3 upload instructions below. We recommend stratified holdout by intent to ensure edge cases are represented; use ~20% per intent bucket. For manual spot-checks we usually review 3–5% of the validation set (prioritized by low confidence or high-impact intents).

Pre-signed S3 details (expires in 7 days):
- Bucket: redwood-poc-uploads-us-west-2
- Prefix: skyline/DL-7832/
- Please upload CSV and logs to the prefix above. Include a small README.txt documenting any sanitation steps and the intent mapping table.

Security notes:
- KMS key: customer-specific CMK (we will request grant once upload completes).
- We will not persist raw prompts to any non-dedicated storage; only the POC evaluation team (Ben/Marcus) will have access.

Eval plan (high-level timeline):
- Thu 2/17: customer uploads CSV + logs to S3 (you estimated EOD)
- Mon 2/21: intake call to confirm receipt and run quick QA + schema validation (20m)
- Week of 2/21: automated eval pass + manual spot-checks (3–4 days)
- Fri 2/25: provisional results and acceptance check-in

Acceptance criteria (for POC):
1) Intent accuracy >=92% on holdout set (stratified)
2) Median token latency <=200ms at sample QPS (we'll replicate with your logs)
3) No unredacted PHI present in the uploaded prompts (customer attestation required)

Owners: Marcus (eval design/infra), Ben (QA scripts & rubric), Naomi (customer comms). Monica is copied in for escalation / procurement coordination if we need entitlements.

If that timeline works I will send the S3 pre-signed URL set after this message.

Thanks,
Marcus

Attachment: upload_instructions.txt (contains S3 presigned URL placeholders)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skylinehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2028 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: prompt/log collection for the POC evaluation (next steps)

On Mon, Feb 21, 2028 at 09:06 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@skylinehealth.com> wrote:
> Marcus / team — files are uploaded to the S3 prefix; README added. Let us know if anything is missing.

Great — I ran the schema validator this morning against sample_prompts_20280214.csv and the logs archive. Quick findings: 

- CSV: 2,476 rows; all required columns present. A handful (~12) of prompts flagged with potential PHI tokens (we redacted in the validator report and left notes in README).
- Logs: token distribution looks slightly heavier on long-form texts (some forms include patient notes). We'll run a tokenization sweep and propose a trimming recommendation if necessary.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Marcus & I will run the automated eval pass (24–48h).
2) Naomi will coordinate a Tuesday 2/28 acceptance sync if we need more time for manual checks.
3) We will send a short rubric spreadsheet showing per-intent thresholds and sample failure cases.

If Skyline can confirm the PHI redaction approach in the README is the final state (and provide the internal mapping table), we can proceed with the automated pass. Otherwise hold on the manual checks until we get the attestation.

Thanks everyone — will update after the automated run completes.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
